headline: GOLD SINKS TO $3,768 — 14-MONTH LOW AS SILVER LOGS SIXTH STRAIGHT SESSION OF LOSSES; $3,700 NOW IN VIEW
snippet: Gold spot fell to $3,768.25 — its lowest level since September 2025 — as of 6:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, while silver logged its sixth consecutive session of losses at $45.74 per ounce. The dual move extends the precious metals selloff that began after October's hot CPI print and deepened through Wednesday's Asian session as the U.S. dollar held near 19-month highs; analysts now identify $3,700 as the next meaningful support with the December 9 FOMC decision the only near-term catalyst for a reversal.

headline: COPPER PLUNGES TO $12,733 — SEVEN-MONTH LOW AS AI DEMAND DOUBTS PILE ON TOP OF HAWKISH FED
snippet: Copper fell 3.7% to $12,733 per tonne on the LME in London's morning session — its lowest level since mid-April — as doubts over AI-driven data centre demand combined with hawkish Fed rate expectations to push the metal below every support level analysts had identified last week. The $13,000 floor that had held through Tuesday's session is now broken, raising new questions about whether the structural copper deficit thesis can survive near-term equity market weakness and tighter financial conditions.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER GET SLAMMED AGAIN — MONEY METALS BREAKS DOWN THREE FORCES DRIVING THE SELLOFF
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's November 16 commentary identifies three converging forces behind the gold and silver selloff: a rising U.S. dollar functioning as the world's safe-haven asset ahead of the December rate hike, global ETF outflows of roughly $1 billion in the first week of November, and a hawkish Fed repricing pushing real yields higher and penalising non-yielding assets. The piece argues that physical coin and bar demand from retail buyers remains firm but is being overwhelmed by financial market selling — a divergence that historically resolves in favour of physical buyers once the rate cycle peaks.

headline: USA RARE EARTH CRUMBLES TO 52-WEEK LOW AT $6.84 — WILLIAM BLAIR CUTS TO MARKET PERFORM; STOCK OFF 70% IN 6 MONTHS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) touched a 52-week low of $6.84 on November 17 — down from its 52-week high of $32.80 — after William Blair cut the stock to Market Perform from Outperform, citing ongoing feedstock shortages and Q3 revenue of $3 million that missed the $13.55 million consensus estimate. The stock has now fallen more than 70% in the past six months, making it the worst-performing name in the rare earth equity complex at a moment when the sector is awaiting a direction signal from the Trump-Xi APEC summit in Shenzhen.

headline: MP MATERIALS Q3 BLOWOUT: REVENUE UP 176%, NdPr PRODUCTION UP 41% — GM MAGNET SHIPMENTS START Q4
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) posted Q3 2026 consolidated revenue of $147.7 million — up 176% year-over-year — with NdPr production of 1,018 metric tons (+41% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.04 versus consensus of a $0.01 loss. The company confirmed it has completed GM qualification for rare earth magnets and expects the first commercial shipments to General Motors in Q4, potentially transforming its revenue profile from a commodity concentrate supplier to a value-added magnet manufacturer — a contrast to the broader rare earth equity selloff.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER DISCOVERS NEW HIGH-GRADE ELENA VEIN AT LA COLORADA — STRUCTURE TRACED 300M ALONG STRIKE
snippet: Pan American Silver (TSX: PAAS) reported the discovery of several new high-grade veins at its La Colorada mine in Zacatecas, Mexico, with the Elena vein — the most significant new structure — traced approximately 300 metres along strike and 300 metres vertically within the established mineralized corridor between the NC2 and San Geronimo veins. The Elena discovery was initially identified from underground exploration development before follow-up drilling confirmed the system's scale, adding resource replacement optionality at one of PAAS's core operating assets.

headline: FREEPORT-McMoRAN SNAPS UP 51% OF TDG GOLD'S AURORA WEST FOR C$110M — BC COPPER-GOLD CONSOLIDATION
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan has agreed to acquire a 51% interest in TDG Gold's Aurora West copper-gold project in British Columbia's Toodoggone district for approximately C$110 million, adding a tier-one operator's endorsement to a junior project in a district Freeport has been systematically assembling. The deal — which still requires TSX Venture Exchange approval — excludes TDG's Shasta and Baker properties and is structured to close after a December reorganisation; for retail investors, Freeport's willingness to pay C$110 million for a 51% stake provides a valuation anchor for comparable early-stage Toodoggone projects.

headline: GENESIS AND VAULT MINERALS COURT-CLEARED TO MERGE — ASX GOLD DEAL IMPLEMENTS NOVEMBER 26
snippet: The Western Australian Supreme Court approved the merger scheme for Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) to acquire all shares in Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU), with the scheme becoming effective November 17 and implementation scheduled for November 26. The deal received 99.74% shareholder support at the November 11 scheme meeting and consolidates two ASX gold producers in a bear market environment where scale and balance sheet strength are becoming key differentiators for investor capital allocation.

headline: URNM MINERS DOWN 31% WHILE URANIUM SPOT HOLDS ABOVE $91 — EQUITY-TO-COMMODITY GAP AT MULTI-YEAR HIGH
snippet: Uranium equity investors are sitting on a 31% year-to-date loss in URNM while physical uranium spot prices hold above $91 per pound — a divergence analysts identify as the largest equity-to-commodity gap in the sector since 2016. The gap is attributed to two converging factors: cost inflation reducing the implied margin advantage of uranium miners, and AI-sector sentiment spillover driving broad selling of energy transition equities regardless of underlying commodity fundamentals.

headline: CHINA TO LAUNCH LITHIUM HYDROXIDE FUTURES NOVEMBER 26 — GUANGZHOU EXCHANGE CREATES FIRST DOMESTIC PRICING BENCHMARK
snippet: The Guangzhou Futures Exchange is set to launch lithium hydroxide futures contracts on November 26, creating China's first domestic standardised pricing benchmark for the key battery input. For mining investors, the launch matters because a transparent domestic price signal should reduce the opacity that has historically complicated lithium project off-take valuations and may eventually serve as the reference price for direct-shipping sales agreements with Chinese battery manufacturers.

headline: ELEVRA LITHIUM CLEARS FINAL PERMIT FOR CAROLINA LITHIUM — NORTH CAROLINA PROJECT NOW FULLY PERMITTED
snippet: Elevra Lithium's Carolina Lithium project in North Carolina has received its final regulatory permit, making it one of the few fully permitted hard-rock lithium development projects in the United States. The milestone is strategically significant at a time of domestic critical minerals policy focus, positioning Carolina Lithium as a potential strategic asset for automakers or battery manufacturers seeking supply-chain security under the Inflation Reduction Act's domestic content requirements.

headline: GOLD BEARS TARGET $3,500 — GDXJ CONFIRMS BREAKDOWN AS MINERS SHOW DOUBLE-LEVERAGE SELLOFF PATTERN
snippet: Analyst Przemyslaw Radomski's November 17 commentary argues that GDXJ's multi-month low, combined with three consecutive down sessions in equities, confirms a technical breakdown in precious metals miners and sets up a move toward $3,500 gold. Radomski identifies an unusually strong stochastic sell signal on miners and argues junior miners are exhibiting classic double-leverage behaviour — selling off with both equities and declining metals — that has historically preceded the most severe drawdowns in the sector.
